subject: Geo-guardrails + TIA scope for MetricsLab procurement redlines
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@metricslab.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@metricslab.ai>, MetricsLab Legal <legal@metricslab.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline + SCC Annex questions (MetricsLab)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our procurement and legal teams took a pass at the DPA and attached a redline (MetricsLab_DPA_redline_v2.docx). A few of the key asks that we need clarity on before we can proceed: 

- They want an SCC annex (or equivalent) that clarifies cross-border flows for model inference, specifically for API traffic that may traverse US <-> EU <-> APAC.
- For APAC customers (notably Japan and Australia) they asked whether Redwood can guarantee onshore processing for certain PII fields or at least a documented fallback routing policy.
- MetricsLab needs a list of subprocessors that may access raw request/response logs and a short attestation about log retention and access controls.
- They also flagged that the TIA/DTIA scope needs to be completed before procurement signs off — they want to include network path diagrams and KMS ownership options (customer-managed or Redwood-managed).

Can you confirm what options we can provide and an estimated timeline? Procurement would like to close the loop by EOD next Wednesday (2028-03-29).

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Director, Strategic Accounts
MetricsLab, Inc.
attachments: MetricsLab_DPA_redline_v2.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@metricslab.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCC Annex questions (MetricsLab)

Amit — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the redline. I grabbed a first pass with engineering/legal to map feasible options. High-level plan below: 

1) TIA scoping: we'll run a focused TIA that covers the inference path (ingest -> runtime -> logs -> storage). I'll attach a small scoping matrix (tia_scoping_matrix.xlsx) so you can confirm boundaries and traffic estimates. We need estimates for qps and the proportion of APAC traffic.

2) Geo-guardrails: we can support routing policies by region (primary region + allowed fallback regions). For strict onshore processing for Japan/Australia we can offer routing-to-region plus a documented fallback to EU only if capacity constraints occur — we'll formalize the SLA and fallback gates in the SCC Annex.

3) Subprocessors: we'll produce an APAC-focused subprocessor list and a short attestation (we use a template internally). If MetricsLab needs continuous attestation or auditor access, we can discuss contractual language.

4) KMS: options are customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed keys with per-customer key separation. Customer-managed KMS will require additional onboarding (about 2–3 weeks) and some network config.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) expected qps and monthly tokens for the pilot, (b) which fields you consider PII that must be onshore, and (c) whether MetricsLab prefers customer-managed KMS? I can coordinate with Marissa + Soojin for legal and security conclusions.

Thanks — I'll pull together the proposed SCC annex language and a TIA statement of work once we have the scoping answers.

— Karthik
Head of Security & Privacy (acting)
Redwood Inference
attachments: tia_scoping_matrix.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@metricslab.ai>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 14:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCC Annex questions (MetricsLab)

Looping in a couple of product/legal notes from our side: 

- On subprocessors: procurement asked to add a clause for real-time access to request/response logs for forensics. We should push back on broad "real-time access" but can offer a formal evidence-handling flow (on-demand with 48-72 hour SLA) and scoped auditor access under NDA.
- For the SCC Annex, let's define a small set of model variants that are permitted in APAC to avoid surprises from cross-region fallbacks (i.e., a quantized local-safe variant + a higher-performance global variant). That allows us to meet their availability needs while limiting data exposure.
- Pricing/ops FYI: customer-managed KMS has a setup fee; legal should mention that in the SOW.

Soojin — would you confirm whether the 48-hour evidence SLA is realistic from infra? Also please flag any additional controls we should list in the SCC Annex (e.g., KV cache segregation, audit trail retention windows).

Marissa
SVP, Product
Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@metricslab.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCC Annex questions (MetricsLab)

Thanks — technical confirmation from Security/Compliance side: 

- Evidence SLA: 48 hours is feasible for a standard evidence request. For live forensics access we'll require a short onboarding checklist and an auditor NDA.
- KMS options: customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS or GCP Cloud KMS are supported. CMK onboarding requires a cross-account IAM mapping + a short validation window (~3 business days). We'll include a checklist in the TIA deliverables.
- SCC/UK IDTA mapping: the SCC Annex will reference both EU SCCs (post-2024 modular clauses) and the UK IDTA addendum where applicable. For each region we'll include an explicit flow diagram and the list of subprocessors with access rationale.
- Subprocessor attestation: attached is our standard template (subprocessor_attestation_template.pdf). For MetricsLab's ask on retention and access restrictions, we can provide per-customer retention overrides, but long-term changes (e.g., under 30-day minimum retention) will require a legal exception.

I'll draft the technical appendix for the SCC Annex (routing rules, fallback gates, KMS onboarding checklist, attestation workflow) and put it in the shared Drive link once Karthik confirms the traffic/PII scope.

Soojin
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
attachments: subprocessor_attestation_template.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@metricslab.ai>, MetricsLab Legal <legal@metricslab.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline + SCC Annex questions (MetricsLab)

Thanks all — quick action plan and owner notes: 

1) Karthik (me) — produce a proposed SCC Annex draft + TIA SOW. Deliverable: draft annex + SOW by 2028-03-24 COB.
2) Marissa — confirm allowed APAC model variants and any pricing notes for CMK onboarding. Please sign-off by 2028-03-25.
3) Soojin — draft technical appendix (routing rules, fallback gates, KMS checklist, attestation flow). Drop in Drive and share link by 2028-03-24.
4) MetricsLab (Amit) — please confirm (a) APAC qps and monthly tokens estimate, (b) fields that must be treated as onshore-only PII, and (c) whether you prefer CMK. Procurement target for signature: 2028-03-29.

Attachments being uploaded to the shared folder and I'll send a DocuSign envelope once we have mutual agreement on the SCC Annex. Preliminary DocuSign link (placeholder): https://docusign.com/abcdef1234567890

Please reply with any blockers. If none, I'll mark this as the active thread and circulate the annex draft tomorrow.

— Karthik
Head of Security & Privacy (acting)
Redwood Inference
